# 270_R6OPS.4 — delayed-job watchdog + hardening (run ledger)

- **Spec:** `docs/tickets/270_R6OPS.4__delayed-job-watchdog.md` (handoff insert — grouping d:
  RH-4 + RH-17 + RH-5 + RH-18 + RH-19). Every finding re-verified against the cited lines this run
  before fixing.
- **Base / branch:** `main` @ `d24dbed8` · branch `stevevitali/r6ops-4-watchdog`, PR base `main`
  (mergePolicy OPERATOR, never merge).
- **Harness:** devin-desktop/swe-2-high/subagent
- **Live stage:** none — Stage A only (code + tests). **Production mutations:** none. **Spend:** $0.

## Finding verdicts (re-verified at tip)

- **RH-4 + RH-17 — CONFIRMED.** `POST /settings/account/delete` stamps `deletion_requested_at` then
  sends `account.hard-delete` with `startAfterMs` = grace end under `singletonKey
  account.hard-delete:<userId>` (`settings-routes.ts`); the send was `.catch(() => undefined)` —
  `ok:true` regardless. Same silent-loss class F-R6WATCH.2-1 proved on `project.purge`: a
  dropped/failed arm leaves the marker forever and nothing notices. Additionally: the api's
  `createQueue` list never created `account.hard-delete` (nor `gate.expiry`/`figure.render`/
  `ingest.*`) — pg-boss 12 `send` to a missing queue inserts zero rows and returns `null` (the
  `insertJobs` `JOIN pgboss.queue` matches nothing) — a send-side silent drop of the same class.
  The marker+send pair is genuinely non-transactional (user row on the app pool, job row on the
  pg-boss system DSN — no shared tx); the honest repair path is the watchdog, not a pretend tx.
- **RH-18 — CONFIRMED, mechanism verified in pg-boss@12.30.0.** Every queue was created `standard`
  policy; the singleton unique indexes are policy-gated (`job_i1` short/`created`, `job_i2`
  singleton/`active`, `job_i3` stately/per-state, `job_i6` exclusive/created+retry+active —
  `plans.js`), so `singletonKey` never conflicted. `create_queue` is `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` and
  `UpdateQueueOptions` omits `policy` — a policy flip cannot ride `createQueue`/`updateQueue` on an
  existing queue. Self-confirming-test trap confirmed: `InMemoryQueue.send` dedupes a keyed send
  against ALL prior sends — strictly stronger than any pg-boss policy — so the "second send is a
  no-op" tests proved intent, never deployed behavior.
- **RH-19 — CONFIRMED.** `account-export-routes.ts` deduped on any `building` row with no staleness
  bound, and a `queue.send` throw after the insert left `building` forever → every later POST
  deduped (wedged user).
- **RH-5 — CONFIRMED, all five arms.** No dup pre-check (unique `user.email` → 500 at confirm), no
  old-address notice, no session revoke, inline unbranded HTML ("Rhema"), plaintext `parsed.token
  !== token` compare with the token stored verbatim.

## Changes

**`apps/worker/src/jobs.ts`** — new `handleAccountDeleteSweep` (the RH-4 watchdog, the
`handleProjectPurgeSweep` pattern): `"user"` rows with `deletion_requested_at` older than 1 h and
no live (`created`/`retry`/`active`) `account.hard-delete` job under `account.hard-delete:<userId>`
are re-armed at their own grace end (`startAfterMs = max(0, requested_at+14d−now)`; send failure
never fails the sweep). Tenant resolved by a lateral `workspace_members` pick (`coalesce` to the
user id — a memberless account is still owed destruction). `handleTestTenantPurge`'s
`account.hard-delete` send now carries the same `singletonKey` — required under `exclusive`
policy (a keyless send shares the `''` singleton slot) and it makes the watchdog's live-arm
check correct for sweep-enqueued arms.

**`apps/worker/src/main.ts`** — (a) `DEDUP_POLICY_QUEUES` (exported): the 15 send-keyed queues
declared `policy: "exclusive"` at `createQueue` (fresh DBs; the prod flip rides migration 0063 —
`createQueue` cannot change an existing row's policy). `exclusive` = at most one
`created`/`retry`/`active` job per singleton key — the send-time dedupe the keys intend; `short`
dedupes only `created`, `singleton` throttles `active` while queueing the duplicate, `stately`
allows one-of-each — none is send dedupe. Scheduled cron queues (`run.reap`, `test-tenant.purge`,
`notify.sweep.*`, `usage.reconcile`, `billing.*`, `ingest.sync.sweep`, `slo.review.weekly`,
`cite.completeness.daily`, run-events retention/partition) and the keyless-send queues
(`mail.send`, `auth.mail`) stay `standard` — a keyless job on an `exclusive` queue dedupes
against every other keyless job via `coalesce(singleton_key,'')`. (b) the sweep rides the
existing hourly `test-tenant.purge` tick beside the project-purge sweep; (c) the
`account.hard-delete` consumer wraps the handler — a throw logs `FAILED` + the user id BEFORE
rethrowing (the 260 loud-loss arm; pg-boss swallows handler throws silently).

**`apps/api/src/server.ts`** — the startup `createQueue` list now covers every queue the api can
send to (`account.hard-delete`, `gate.expiry`, `figure.render`, `ingest.sync`,
`ingest.reconstruct`, `voice.purge` added) and declares `exclusive` on the same dedupe set —
whichever process creates a queue first lands the intended policy.

**`packages/db/migrations/0063_pgboss_queue_policies.sql`** — `update pgboss.queue set
policy='exclusive'` on the 15 dedupe queues, guarded by `to_regclass('pgboss.queue')` (pg-boss
self-migrates its schema; migration-only test DBs carry none). Policy stamps onto each job at
insert — pre-existing `standard` jobs keep old semantics (the watchdog `not exists` checks are
policy-blind; transition-window duplicate arms are handler-idempotent no-ops). Additive-lint clean.

**`apps/api/src/settings-routes.ts`** — RH-17: the hard-delete enqueue failure logs
`console.error("[api] account.hard-delete enqueue FAILED for user <id> — the watchdog sweep
re-arms within the hour:", err)` (the 260 FAILED+id shape; `ok:true` stays honest — the marker is
the state, the sweep repairs). RH-5, all five arms: (1) `email_taken` 409 pre-check at request +
a `23505` catch at confirm (TOCTOU); (2) old-address `auth.mail` notices at request
("being changed") AND completion ("was changed"); (3) confirm deletes every OTHER session
(`token <> current-cookie-token`; the confirming session survives — it just proved the new
mailbox); (4) branded `Rhēma` templates in `magic-link-email.ts`
(`renderEmailChangeVerifyEmail`/`renderEmailChangeNoticeEmail`); (5) the verification row stores
`tokenHash` (SHA-256) and confirm compares with `crypto.timingSafeEqual` — legacy `token` rows
(≤1 h TTL overlap) still confirm via the hashed path.

**`apps/api/src/magic-link-email.ts`** — the two new renderers, same branded card shell (macron
`Rhēma`; token only in the URL; no link in the notice).

**`apps/api/src/account-export-routes.ts`** — RH-19: `ACCOUNT_EXPORT_BUILDING_STALE_MS = 1 h`
(a legit build is bounded by `expire_seconds` 15 min × retries plus queue wait). A `building`
row older than the bound is marked `failed` (`build_expired`) instead of deduping forever; a
`queue.send` throw marks the new row `failed` (`enqueue_failed`) and answers 503 — the next POST
builds fresh.

**`apps/api/src/ingest-routes.ts`** — `voice.purge` send gains `singletonKey:
voice.purge:<personaId>` (the `exclusive` queue requires keys; the dedupe was also intended).

**`packages/orchestrator/src/queue.ts`** — `InMemoryQueue` docstring names the self-confirming
trap: it models the intent (dedupe against all prior sends), not pg-boss's state machine.

## Judgement calls

- **`exclusive` over `stately`/`singleton`:** the send sites document "a duplicate/replay is a
  no-op" — send-time dedupe, which only `exclusive` provides across `created`/`retry`/`active`.
- **Policy flip needs the migration:** `create_queue` is `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` and `updateQueue`
  omits `policy` (pg-boss@12.30.0 verified) — code declarations cover fresh DBs; 0063 flips prod's
  existing rows at the next migrate leg. Existing `standard`-stamped jobs keep inert keys
  (transition-window dup arms are handler-idempotent).
- **`ok:true` retained on the delete route:** the marker row is the state and the hourly sweep is
  the repair — honest. The marker+send pair cannot share a transaction (app pool vs pg-boss DSN);
  a real fix is the outbox pattern → BACKLOG `BL-115` (sibling row, as the ticket offered).
- **Session revoke keeps the confirming session** (the better-auth `revokeOtherSessions`
  semantic): the confirm itself rides that session after proving the new mailbox; the old-address
  notices are the takeover arm.
- **Old-address notice sent at BOTH request and completion:** request-time is the anti-takeover
  arm (the incumbent learns before the new mailbox can confirm); completion is the recovery arm.
- **TTL = 1 h** for `building` staleness (job expire 15 min × `retry_limit` 2 + queue wait).
- **No `system-pool-boundary` change:** the sweep lives in `apps/worker/src/jobs.ts`, an already
  allowlisted file; no new tenant read (the `"user"`/`workspace_members`/`pgboss.job` scan is the
  same cross-tenant class the file's existing sweeps run).
- **Manifest:** rows 266–277 + `GD-HANDOFF.R6` ride PR #344 (`stevevitali/rh-inserts`) — not
  duplicated here (identical bytes would collide; the row is the insert PR's).
